Report_ID: Distal expressive second-language (English) vocabulary — EVT-2 standard score at posttest
Title: The effects of content-related shared book reading on the language development of preschool dual language learners
Author: Pollard-Durodola, Gonzalez, Saenz, Soares, Resendez, Kwok, Davis, & Zhu
Comment: Cluster-randomised trial (randomisation at classroom level; 252 children in 42 classrooms, ~6 children per class). Table 2 means/SDs/Ns are NOT cluster-adjusted; the paper reports an EVT-2 posttest ICC of 27.57% (0.2757), so a design-effect adjustment of 1 + (6-1)*0.2757 = 2.38 would be applied downstream using the PAPER-REPORTED ICC (not the assumed 0.15). The paper's own cluster-adjusted multilevel estimate for the intervention effect is γ01 = -0.58 (SE = 2.38), p = 0.980 (Table 3), adjusted for pretest and child/teacher covariates; this was not entered into M_diff/SE_diff to avoid mixing it with the raw group means recorded here. M_diff not computed because of the multilevel/cluster design and to avoid sign ambiguity (group_1 is the intervention arm, matching the paper's table order). Cohen's d printed as -0.04 in Table 2 (text writes "0.04" without the sign).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Content-enriched interactive shared book reading intervention (Project WORLD)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: early childhood language/vocabulary intervention, dual language learners
Topic of Content: Science and social studies content-related vocabulary via thematically paired storybooks and informational texts
Participant type: Spanish-speaking preschool dual language learners (mean age ~56 months) in one-way dual language bilingual prekindergarten programs
Recruitment source: All elementary schools with preschool dual language bilingual programs (n = 23) in two high-poverty Texas school districts
Outcome measurement: Posttest EVT-2 standard scores (means and SDs by condition, Table 2)
Outcome variable: Distal expressive second-language (English) vocabulary — EVT-2 standard score at posttest
effect_direction: favours control (negligible; d = -0.04, intervention 63.65 vs control 64.60)

Report_ID: EOWPVT raw score at posttreatment (distal expressive French/L2 vocabulary)
Title: Monolingual or Bilingual Intervention for Primary Language Impairment? A Randomized Control Trial
Author: Thordardottir, Cloutier, Ménard, Pelland-Blais, & Rvachew
Comment: Three-arm trial: the monolingual French (L2-only) treatment arm was selected as the intervention group because it matches the review's L2 vocabulary-teaching definition; the bilingual arm is recorded in additional_group_ns and the control arm is used once. Groups were NOT equivalent at baseline on this measure — the control group scored significantly higher than both treatment groups at intake (EOWPVT pre: MT 6.1, BT 6.3, NT 12.0), so the raw post-test comparison is confounded. The paper reports only that the ANOVA of pre–post difference scores showed no significant group differences; no exact F, p, or effect size is given for the EOWPVT, so no test statistic was recorded. M_diff not computed because the design is a three-group ANOVA rather than a simple two-group comparison.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Monolingual French focused-stimulation treatment (MT)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: bilingual preschool children (mean age 59.56 months) with primary language impairment, minority home language with French as L2
Recruitment source: speech-language pathology departments of two Montréal hospitals, a rehabilitation centre, and French public schools
Outcome measurement: Raw score on standardized expressive picture-naming test, posttreatment assessment immediately following the 16-week intervention period, administered by a blinded research assistant
Outcome variable: EOWPVT raw score at posttreatment (distal expressive French/L2 vocabulary)
additional_group_ns: Bilingual treatment (BT) arm not selected for this row: n = 9, posttreatment EOWPVT M = 9.7 (SD = 4.0), pretreatment M = 6.3 (SD = 3.1)
effect_direction: favours control (post-test 11.1 intervention vs 12.9 no-treatment control, but control started higher at baseline)

Report_ID: Expressive second-language (Norwegian) vocabulary, distal standardized measure (WPPSI/WISC vocabulary) at post-test 1
Title: Improving the General Language Skills of Second-Language Learners in Kindergarten: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Rogde, Melby-Lervåg & Lervåg
Comment: Per-arm Ns are not printed in Table 1; they were taken from the Methods/Participants gender counts ("intervention group (34 boys, 24 girls)" = 58; "control group (34 boys, 23 girls)" = 57) and may differ slightly from the final analysed N at t2 (missing data were handled with maximum-likelihood estimation). The reported d = .55 (p = .000) is a y-standardized latent-variable coefficient for the EXPRESSIVE LANGUAGE FACTOR (expressive vocabulary + expressive grammar + narrative retelling) controlling for pre-test, not a raw post-test SMD for the WPPSI/WISC vocabulary measure alone; it is recorded for reference only. M_diff not computed (group_1 is the intervention arm; raw means/SDs supplied instead). Randomization was at the individual child level with Huber-White correction for kindergarten dependency, so no design-effect adjustment was applied.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('18-week general language intervention (dialogic reading, explicit tier-2 word teaching, grammar, narrative training; 54 sessions)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: education / language intervention for second-language learners
Study Environment: kindergarten classrooms; individual testing in Norwegian by trained research assistants
Content length: 18 weeks, 54 sessions (two 40-45 min small-group sessions and one 10-min individual session per week)
Topic of Content: general language skills: vocabulary, grammar, narrative; dialogic storybook reading
Participant type: Second-language learners in the final year of kindergarten (mean age 66.18 months, SD = 3.47), both parents with a first language other than Norwegian
Recruitment source: 31 kindergartens (55 classes) in two suburban municipalities in Norway
Outcome measurement: Raw score mean and SD at Time 2 (post-test 1), Table 1
Outcome variable: Expressive second-language (Norwegian) vocabulary, distal standardized measure (WPPSI/WISC vocabulary) at post-test 1

Report_ID: Expressive second-language (English) vocabulary — WLPB-R Picture Vocabulary raw score at post-test (end of Grade 1)
Title: Accelerating Early Academic Oral English Development in Transitional Bilingual and Structured English Immersion Programs
Author: Tong, Lara-Alecio, Irby, Mathes, & Kwok
Comment: No inferential test of PV3 between groups is reported by the paper — only descriptive means/SDs (Table 1); the inferential analyses (Tables 7-8) pertain to the PV+LC composite latent growth parameters, which do not match the planned outcome. M_diff/effect size therefore not computed here per the value-validity rules. Design is school-randomised/cluster-based (23 schools, 60 classrooms) and no cluster-adjusted estimates are reported for PV3, so a design-effect adjustment to n (assumed ICC 0.15) would be required downstream; raw per-arm n are recorded as reported. Student-level assignment was quasi-experimental (schools randomized), and children were ~7 years old at post-test (mean age 67.13 months at kindergarten baseline), which may fall outside the review's randomised/≤6-years eligibility criteria.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('TBE-E (transitional bilingual education, enhanced/experimental oral English intervention)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Design Type: quasi_experimental (school-level random assignment, student-level quasi-experimental), 2-year longitudinal
Country: United States (urban school district, southeastern Texas)
Participant type: Hispanic, native Spanish-speaking English-language learners (kindergarten to end of first grade)
Recruitment source: 23 elementary schools / 60 classrooms in one urban school district in southeastern Texas
Outcome measurement: Post-test (spring 2006) group means and standard deviations of PV3 raw scores, Table 1
Outcome variable: Expressive second-language (English) vocabulary — WLPB-R Picture Vocabulary raw score at post-test (end of Grade 1)
additional_group_ns: Not used in this row (second program type, reported separately in Table 1): SEI-E (enhanced structured English immersion) n = 88, PV3 M = 24.341, SD = 2.963; SEI-T (typical structured English immersion control) n = 125, PV3 M = 24.176, SD = 5.055. The TBE pair was selected as the single effect for this trial because it is the larger subsample and because PV3 for SEI-T badly violated normality (skewness -2.781, kurtosis 11.263).
effect_direction: favours intervention (20.52 vs 19.50 at end of Grade 1)

Report_ID: English (L2) Definitional Vocabulary posttest adjusted score — English-only intervention vs. business-as-usual control
Title: Do Early Literacy Skills in Children's First Language Promote Development of Skills in Their Second Language? An Experimental Evaluation of Transfer
Author: Goodrich, Lonigan, & Farver
Comment: Means are age-ADJUSTED posttest means (Table 2), not raw posttest means — noted per plan. Per-arm n is NOT reported in the paper; only total N = 94 across three arms and N = 63 for this pairwise contrast, so group_1_n/group_2_n left empty rather than invented. M_diff not computed because this is a 3-arm design with age-adjusted means (means do not come from a simple unadjusted two-group comparison). The reported beta (.19) comes from the FINAL (Step 3) regression model containing interaction terms, per the table title. The Definitional Vocabulary subtest combines an expressive naming part and a definitional part; only the composite subtest score is reported. Randomization was of individual children within 10 classrooms; the paper reports no ICC and no cluster adjustment.; regression: no convertible statistic — need t-value for coefficient, b+SE(b), standardised β, r, η², or means+SDs
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (3-arm), secondary moderation analysis
Participant type: Spanish-speaking language-minority preschool children (Head Start), mean age 54.51 months (SD = 4.72)
Recruitment source: 10 classes in a Head Start center in Los Angeles, California
Outcome measurement: Adjusted M (SD) at posttest, adjusted for chronological age (Table 2); standardized regression coefficient for intervention condition main effect (Table 4, Step 1)
Outcome variable: English (L2) Definitional Vocabulary posttest adjusted score — English-only intervention vs. business-as-usual control
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: Transitional (Spanish-to-English) Literacy Express condition, English Definitional Vocabulary posttest adjusted M = 52.28 (SD = 12.07); extracted as a separate row. Per-arm sample sizes are not reported anywhere in the paper (only total N = 94 and N = 63 for each pairwise contrast).
effect_direction: favours intervention (English-only arm 47.45 vs control 41.23; note control is group_1 in this row)

Report_ID: Expressive vocabulary in the second language (Mandarin Chinese) - EVT Chinese raw score at post-test
Title: The efficacy of a school-based book-reading intervention on vocabulary development of young Uyghur children: A randomized controlled trial
Author: Chen, Lawrence, Zhou, Min, & Snow
Comment: p_value field records only that the paper reported the treatment effect as non-significant (p > 0.05) for the XJP x T growth-rate coefficient (gamma11 = 0.02, SE = 1.09, Table 4 Model 2); no exact p-value is given. M_diff/SE_diff left empty: the paper's own inferential analysis is a multilevel growth model of change rate, not a simple post-test mean contrast, so a difference of the Table 3 descriptive means was not computed. Ns reflect final analysed sample at wave 3 (17 children lost to attrition from the 134/122 randomised).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('The Xinjiang Project (XJP) book-reading intervention classes') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Participant type: Uyghur-speaking 4-5-year-old kindergarten children learning Mandarin Chinese as a second language
Recruitment source: 12 public bilingual kindergartens (31 classes) in Urumqi and Turpan, Xinjiang, China

Report_ID: E EV CELF — English (L2) distal expressive vocabulary, posttest
Title: Early Efficacy of Multitiered Dual-Language Instruction: Promoting Preschoolers' Spanish and English Oral Language
Author: Spencer, Moran, Thompson, Petersen, & Restrepo
Comment: Cluster-randomized trial; the reported estimate, CI and Hedges' g come from a random-intercept ANCOVA adjusting for pretest (posttest ICC = .09), i.e. cluster-adjusted model-based values. Table 3 posttest M(SD) are UNADJUSTED; adjusted posttest means (7.21 vs 7.47) are reported without SDs/SEs, so unadjusted SDs are paired with them here. SE_diff derived from the reported 95% CI as (1.86 − (−2.38))/3.92 = 1.08; M_diff is the paper's own reported estimated adjusted mean difference (treatment − control), not computed from the table means.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Treatment: multitiered dual-language instruction (Puente de Cuentos), 12 classrooms') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: early childhood language intervention / dual-language learners
Content length: full school year (three units of 8–10 weeks each)
Topic of Content: multitiered dual-language narrative and vocabulary curriculum (Puente de Cuentos)
Participant type: 3- to 5-year-old Head Start preschoolers from Spanish-speaking homes learning English
Recruitment source: Head Start centers (one urban, one rural) in a southwestern U.S. state
Outcome measurement: Raw score on CELF-P English Expressive Vocabulary subtest at posttest (April/May), analyzed with random-intercept ANCOVA adjusting for pretest
Outcome variable: E EV CELF — English (L2) distal expressive vocabulary, posttest
effect_direction: favours control (adjusted mean difference -0.26, Hedges g = -0.05)
